title: Twitter began as a side project at a podcast company
summary: Odeo built a podcasting platform until Apple added podcasts to iTunes in fall 2005. A text-based side project, Twttr, launched publicly on July 15, 2006. Two months later it had fewer than 5,000 registered users.

beats.say: Twitter began as a side project at a podcast company.
beats.cap: Twitter began at a podcast company

beats.say: That company, Odeo, had built a podcasting platform by July two thousand five.
In fall two thousand five, Apple announced iTunes with built in podcasting.
Odeo's podcasting focus lost its relevance, and it had fourteen full time employees.
In February two thousand six, three people presented a text based idea called Twttr.
Twttr launched to the public on July fifteenth, two thousand six.
Messages were capped at one hundred forty characters, based on text message limits.
By September two thousand six, it had fewer than five thousand registered users.
In November two thousand thirteen, Twitter went public, valued at just over thirty one billion dollars.
A podcast company's side project became a public company.

claims.note: NBC News: Odeo had 14 full-time employees at that point
HISTORY: Odeo released Twttr to the public on July 15, 2006
HISTORY: the 140-character limit was based on the maximum length of text messages at the time
NBC News: in September 2006 a letter to Odeo's investors said Twitter had less than 5,000 registered users
HISTORY: when the company went public in November 2013 it was valued at just over $31 billion
